intent: Fix two runtime defects the analyze_repo.sh split introduced in 41cc045, both of which every static check passed clean, and verify the fix by running the script end to end against the pre-split original.
scope: Non-goal: any further restructuring; the seam from 41cc045 is unchanged
changes: Renamed the nameref locals from LANG_CODE_FILES to _code_files in both libs. A nameref whose local name equals the global it points at is a self-reference: bash 5.3 still moves the data, but warns 'circular name reference' on every single access, and those warnings land in this script's user-facing output.

Replaced the entry's bare `declare -A LANG_CODE_FILES` plus two literal call arguments with a CODE_FILES_MAP variable holding the name. After the rename shellcheck could no longer see the array as used (SC2034), because it was only ever mentioned as a bare word; passing it through a variable makes the reference real rather than suppressing the warning.

Added `|| true` to the eight `((LANG_FILES[x] > 0)) && HAS_Y=true` lines in detect_languages. These were top-level statements before the split, where a false `((...)) &&` merely left $? non-zero. As the tail of a function they become its return value, and under `set -e` the last one -- java, false for most repositories -- aborted the entire script immediately after language detection.

verification.command: bash <stubbed entry> <fixture repo> <outdir>, against the same run from a detached worktree at 133fccf (pre-split)
verification.evidence: Pre-split exits 0 and completes. The split as committed in 41cc045 exited 1 immediately after 'Files found by language', producing none of STEPs 5-8. After the fix it exits 0 and reaches the final summary, with zero 'circular name reference' warnings (was one per map access).

verification.command: diff of every generated artifact, pre-split run vs fixed run
verification.evidence: Identical file set, and every text artifact byte-identical: tokei_stats, scc_stats, scc_complexity, code_identifiers, comment_words, grep_keywords, grep_function_calls, grep_imports, the per_language/* files, tags, ctags_symbols, ctags_kinds and cscope.files. Only cscope.out.in differs, in binary hash-table padding; its input list cscope.files is identical and both indexes are the same 90112 bytes.
Zero findings, no suppression added. The SC2034 introduced by the rename was fixed by making the reference real, not by silencing it.

verification.command: audit of every wrapped function's last statement for the same set -e hazard
verification.evidence: detect_languages was the only one ending in a conditional. analyze_symbols and analyze_cscope end in 'fi', analyze_clang_ast and separate_code_and_comments in echo, report_languages in a command already carrying '|| true'. Confirmed by the end-to-end run reaching the final summary.
entry 234, report 228, separate 193, symbols 112, tools 124, scan 86. All six still under the cap after the added lines.

risks: Both defects were invisible to bash -n, shellcheck, the function-set diff, the line-set diff and the stubbed source run -- that last one sources the libs but never calls the functions, so it could not reach either bug. The general lesson is that a stubbed run proves the source lines resolve and nothing more; only a real execution exercises a seam that passes state.

The fixture repository used for the comparison contains one Python and one C file, so the java/ruby/go/rust/shell branches of separate_code_and_comments were not executed. They are structurally identical to the two that were, and the line-set diff shows they differ from the original only by the mechanical rename.
install_missing_tools was stubbed for both runs, so the package-installation path remains unexecuted under decision 6. It is unchanged by this commit.
rollback: git revert this commit to return to 41cc045's state -- but note that state is the broken one: the script aborts after language detection. A rollback should go to 133fccf, reverting the split itself.
After rollback, re-run the script against a small fixture repo and confirm it exits 0 and prints the STEP 8 summary.
